title: The Failed Payment Spike
description:
**SITUATION:**

Finance team saw more card payments fail yesterday than on a normal day. The dashboard they already have never captured how each failure was written, and the details around the failed payments. The payments lead wants those numbers from the raw **payment-handler** log, `/var/log/payment-handler/payments.log`.

**Counting the failures.** The same event is written `FAILED`, `Failed`, and `failed`, and finance wants every one of those lines, in the order they were written to be captured. Decline codes are just as messy: `E402` and `E4021` look alike but mean different things, and you should count the right one, counting the wrong one sends finance after the wrong batch.

**Which orders were declined.** An order ID is `ORD-` followed by 6 digits, and it only counts on a line that says **declined**. Along-side you also see entries with **predeclined**, it is a screening pass, not a decline, and the same order can appear more than once.

**Where the timeout is set.** The timeout is not in one file. Configs are spread through `/etc/payment-handler` and the folders under it. A real setting assigns a value, and the name varies: `timeout = 12s`, `read_timeout = 5s`, or `connect_timeout = 3s`. A comment that mentions these timeouts won't count here.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Save every line from `/var/log/payment-handler/payments.log` that says **failed**, in any letter case, to `~/answers/failed.txt`.
2. Count the lines with decline code **E402** exactly (`E4021` is a different code) and save the number in `~/answers/e402-count`.
3. Save the unique order IDs (`ORD-` and 6 digits) from lines with the word **declined** to `~/answers/declined-orders`.
4. Save the full paths of the configs under `/etc/payment-handler` that assign a timeout (`timeout`, `read_timeout`, or `connect_timeout`) to `~/answers/timeout-configs`. A comment that only mentions the word does not count.

**SPEC:**

- `~/answers/failed.txt`: the matching lines, unchanged and in log order
- `~/answers/e402-count`: just the number of `E402` lines
- `~/answers/declined-orders`: one order ID per line, no duplicates
- `~/answers/timeout-configs`: full paths of the configs that set a timeout, one per line

**REFERENCES:**

- [DevSetu Blog — Read, Edit and Search Text: less, tail, vi, grep](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/reading-and-searching-text)
- [DevSetu Blog — Edit: sed for one-line changes](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/reading-and-searching-text#sed-in-place)
- [DevSetu Blog — Pipes and Pipelines: sort, uniq, wc, cut, awk](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/pipes-and-pipelines)

hints: You are learner on a real Ubuntu machine with systemd; sudo works without a password.
Reset gives you a fresh machine (your changes are wiped).
Read SPEC carefully, then Submit — the grader checks the machine itself.
problemStatement.solution:
Finance wants the numbers from the raw payment-handler log, not from a dashboard. `grep` prints the lines that match a pattern. This log has four traps: letter case, a code that is the start of a longer code, a word sitting inside a longer word, and a comment that mentions timeout without setting it.

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-i` | Ignores letter case |
| `-w` | Matches a whole word, so `E402` does not match `E4021` |
| `-c` | Counts matching lines |
| `-o` | Prints only the matched text |
| `-E` | Extended patterns, such as `{6}` |
| `-r` | Searches every file under a directory |
| `-l` | Prints the names of files that match |

```bash
cd /var/log/payment-handler
mkdir -p ~/answers
```

## 1. Every failed payment, in any case

```bash
grep -i 'failed' payments.log > ~/answers/failed.txt
```

`-i` keeps `FAILED`, `Failed`, and `failed`. The lines stay in log order.

## 2. How many E402s

```bash
grep -cw 'code=E402' payments.log > ~/answers/e402-count
```

Without `-w`, `E402` also matches `E4021`. The file should contain the number alone.

## 3. Unique order IDs on declined lines

```bash
grep -w 'declined' payments.log | grep -oE 'ORD-[0-9]{6}' | sort -u > ~/answers/declined-orders
```

The first `grep` keeps declined lines and skips `predeclined`. The second cuts out the order IDs. `sort -u` drops duplicates.

## 4. Configs that set a timeout

```bash
grep -rlE '^[a-z_]*timeout *=' /etc/payment-handler > ~/answers/timeout-configs
```

The name is not always `read_timeout`. The same line can be `timeout = 12s`, `read_timeout = 5s`, or `connect_timeout = 3s`. `^` means the match starts at the beginning of the line, so a comment like `# Timeouts are configured per gateway` is left out.

Then **Submit**.
